differences.title: 1. MEMORY MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Zig provides explicit control over memory allocation via arenas and manual calls, empowering developers to fine-tune performance and avoid runtime overhead.
differences.rightDesc: Rust enforces memory safety at compile time through its ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes system, eliminating data races and use-after-free bugs.

differences.title: 2. ERROR HANDLING
differences.leftDesc: Zig utilizes error union types, where functions return either a success value or an error value, promoting explicit error propagation.
differences.rightDesc: Rust uses the `Result<T, E>` enum, forcing developers to handle potential errors explicitly, making failure pathways clear and robust.

differences.title: 3. COMPILE-TIME EXECUTION
differences.leftDesc: Zig's 'comptime' allows arbitrary code execution during compilation, enabling meta-programming, compile-time checks, and generic code generation.
differences.rightDesc: Rust leverages powerful procedural macros and declarative macros for compile-time code generation, metaprogramming, and DSLs, enhancing expressiveness.

differences.title: 4. ABSTRACTION LEVEL
differences.leftDesc: Zig prioritizes simplicity and a minimal set of core features, aiming for a low-level feel akin to C but with modern tooling.
differences.rightDesc: Rust offers higher-level abstractions like traits and generics, enabling expressive and reusable code without sacrificing performance.

differences.title: 5. BUILD SYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Zig has a built-in, powerful build system that simplifies cross-compilation, dependency management, and project configuration directly within the language.
differences.rightDesc: Rust's `Cargo` is a sophisticated package manager and build tool, handling dependencies, testing, and cross-compilation seamlessly.

differences.title: 6. TARGET ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Zig excels at C ABI compatibility, making it ideal for extending C projects or replacing C codebases with easier integration.
differences.rightDesc: Rust has first-class support for WebAssembly, enabling high-performance browser applications and serverless functions with a mature toolchain.

differences.title: 7. COMMUNITY & MATURITY
differences.leftDesc: Zig is younger, rapidly evolving, with a smaller but passionate community contributing to its innovative features and ecosystem growth.
differences.rightDesc: Rust boasts a large, active community, extensive libraries (crates.io), and a proven track record in various industries, signifying maturity.
